newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB analyst "surprised" by higher EU barley rebate.
newsitem.headline: CWB analyst "surprised" by higher EU barley rebate.

text.p: An increase in European Union rebates on barley exports on Thursday was "surprising" and next week's export licences will be watched closely, a Canadian Wheat Board market analyst said.

"The refund's slightly higher than last week and it's a bit surprising since they (European Union) are really the only players in the market right now, but it's a small amount of barley," CWB Western Europe market analyst Peter Watts told Reuters.
The EU granted a 29.79 ECU a tonne rebate on 26,000 tonnes of barley, about US$132/tonne FOB France, Watts said.
"I understand most of it's from Germany and a lot is malting barley," Watts said.

The Canadian government earlier Thursday approved a C$8 to C$20 a tonne increase to CWB initial prices for malting barley but that decision likely had no bearing on the EU's hike in its export rebate, Watts said.
"The Europeans are the only ones in the market right now. Australia has the same logistical constraints as us right now," he said.
French barley traders on Thursday were bidding for rebates between 30.45 and 31.95 ECUs, Watts added.

"The (European) Commission didn't accept any French bids because they were too aggressive, which means the Commission doesn't want to go below US$132, so we'll have to see what happens next week," Watts said.
The increase in rebate was also a surprise because of the EU's ability to supply the Saudi Arabian market, which traditionally buys at least 40 percent of the world market in feed barley, he added.
"The European traders are short possibly as much as 800,000 tonnes to Saudi Arabia," Watts said.
